description: A small, ubiquitous European lawn flower with white ray florets and a yellow disc.
Deep tap-rooted pioneer species; every part of the plant is edible.
Host plant for peacock and small tortoiseshell butterflies.
Nitrogen-fixing legume, critical to pollinators in urban lawns.
Reddish-stemmed street-crack inhabitant with a distinctive musky scent.
Tall spire of tubular flowers; highly toxic, medicinally important.
A rare sight in urban settings; appears briefly in spring.
